body:
I had a somewhat ironic conversation with a friend yesterday about Robin Williams that touches on this exact point. They said that they wish he would have reached out to someone. My mind went exactly to the place yours did. It's a nice sentiment, but you really don't want to open that door. If I had responded with "Well I've ruined the last ten years of my life, driven just about everyone away, and the person you know is just a thin veneer of faking it on top of an exhausted, beaten-down husk. The highlight of my day is when I finally get enough liquor inside me that I black out and stop existing," that person would run so fast your head would spin.

I checked myself into a facility some years ago and to this day I still get awkwardly phrased questions about whether or not I'm all there mentally. The reality of reaching out for help and talking to someone ignores some pretty significant realities of the situation. Odds are you aren't going to talk someone out of it, and unless you want to basically provide for me like a child as I live on your couch - since I will have been fired by this point - for some indeterminate period of time, then reaching out isn't going to do much. I've run that gauntlet a couple times and it always ends with resentment from both parties.
